Heavy Rainfall Warning No. 63 #NCR_PRSD
Weather System: Enhanced Southwest Monsoon (Habagat)
Issued at: 11:00 AM, 25 July 2025(Friday)

YELLOW WARNING LEVEL: Metro Manila, Bataan, Rizal, Zambales, Batangas, Cavite, Bulacan and Pampanga.
ASSOCIATED HAZARD: FLOODING in flood-prone areas.
Meanwhile, expect light to moderate with occasional heavy rains over Tarlac and Nueva Ecija within the next 3 hours.
Light to moderate with occasional heavy rains affecting Laguna(Santa Cruz, Majayjay, Magdalena, Victoria, Los Banos, Calamba, Cabuyao, Santa Rosa, Binan, San Pedro, Bay, Calauan, Alaminos, San Pablo, Rizal, Nagcarlan, Liliw, Pila) and Quezon(Lucban, Tayabas, Lucena, Candelaria, Tiaong, San Antonio, Dolores, Sariaya, Pagbilao) which may persist within 3 hours and may affect nearby areas.

The public and the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices concerned are advised to MONITOR the weather condition and watch for the next warning to be issued at 2:00 PM today.
For more information and queries, please call telephone numbers 8927-1335 and 8927-2877 or log on to https://t.co/59mTpZISbP.

data.raw_text:
LEGARDA URGES STRICT ENFORCEMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL LAWS AMID WORSENING FLOODS

Senator Loren Legarda has called for the urgent and strict enforcement of environmental laws, particularly Republic Act No. 9003 or the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act, as severe flooding continues to affect Metro Manila and other parts of the country due to the southwest monsoon.

"We are drowning in our own waste and garbage," said Legarda, principal author of RA 9003, as she pointed to clogged waterways and poor waste management as key contributors to recurring floods.

She warned that the failure to comply with solid waste laws and the continued environmental neglect pose serious threats to communities, especially during heavy rains. "Flooding is not just a matter of inconvenience; it puts our families, our children, our neighbors, and our kababayans' lives at risk. We cannot expect safe, clean, and flood-free communities if we continue to disregard basic environmental rules," she added.

Legarda also cited illegal structures on waterways and weak enforcement at the community level as factors that worsen flooding. "Marami sa mga daluyan ng tubig, kanal, estero, at maging mga ilog ay tinayuan ng bahay, gusali, at istrukturang gawa sa semento at aspalto," she said. "Patuloy tayong nalulubog dahil din sa ating kapabayaan."

She called on local government units, the MMDA, and national agencies to intensify the rehabilitation of esteros and flood-prone areas, and urged citizens to actively participate in barangay cleanup drives. "Flood management is not just a government responsibility. As citizens, we also have to do our part," she said.

Legarda also appealed to the maritime sector to stop dumping waste into the sea, saying monsoon currents carry marine litter to coastal communities. "Our seas, oceans, and rivers are waters that sustain life—they are not trash bins," she said.

As a longtime environmental advocate, Legarda reiterated that flooding and extreme weather events are worsening due to the climate crisis. She is the principal author of the Climate Change Act of 2009 and recently chaired a high-level meeting of the Climate Vulnerable Forum, where she called on global leaders to ramp up climate finance and resilience efforts.

Legarda said environmental protection remains key to disaster preparedness and sustainable development.

WIDESPREAD RAIN, FLOOD THREATS ACROSS LUZON DUE TO EMONG, HABAGAT

PAGASA hoisted a Red Rainfall Warning in Benguet as Severe Tropical Storm #EmongPH and the enhanced southwest monsoon continue to dump torrential rains across Luzon.

Orange Warning: La Union
Yellow Warning: Metro Manila, Bataan, Rizal, Zambales, Batangas, Cavite, Bulacan, Pampanga, Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, Pangasinan, Abra, Apayao

Flooding and landslides are possible in affected areas.

Light to heavy rain is also hitting parts of Laguna, Quezon, Nueva Vizcaya, Ifugao, Mt. Province, Kalinga, Quirino, and Cagayan, and may persist in Batanes, Isabela, and Aurora in the next 2–3 hours.
